title: O the Almighty Lord
description: O the Almighty Lord in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 80, headed “God's awful power and goodness”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O the Al-might-y Lord! How match-less is his power! Trem-ble, O earth, be-neath his word, And all the heavens a-dore.

lines: Tremble, O earth, beneath his word,
Crouch to his feet, ye haughty things,
Or he shall tread you down.
We love to speak thy praise;
Thy sceptre's equal to thy rod,
And heavenly mercy walls us round
Thus we adore the God of might,
And bless the God of love.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
